fatal_errors: Misidentifies the initial material as a single-phase solid solution rather than as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC and B2 phases.
Omits the controlling intervention: intermediate-temperature aging, particularly at approximately 600°C and 750°C.
Does not predict the non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
Provides a circular mechanism in which crack initiation is invoked to explain crack initiation.
Omits L12 ordering, increased APBE and modulus, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, and phase-boundary stress concentration.
Defines no quantitative aging-temperature or loading boundaries.
explanation: The response only captures the generic possibility of localized deformation and brittle fracture under severe loading. It does not reconstruct the thermally induced mechanism or the governing 550–750°C aging window. The proposed experiments could document mechanical degradation, but they do not specifically discriminate the target mechanism from conventional grain-boundary embrittlement or other fracture mechanisms; they lack measurements of ordering, phase-boundary morphology, dislocation pile-ups at jagged boundary tips, and impurity segregation. The falsification rule is also weak because it merely negates the predicted outcome rather than testing the proposed causal pathway.
